capabilities.name: shell.introspect
capabilities.description: Enumerate builtins, their argument and return types, and their declared effect. The ontology is machine-discoverable without documentation scraping.

capabilities.name: shell.eval
capabilities.description: Evaluate AetherShell source. Reaches every other capability here, so it is governed at the effect of whatever it evaluates, not at the effect of evaluation.

capabilities.name: fs.read
capabilities.description: Read local state: file contents, directory listings, process listings, environment. Effect::ReadLocal.

capabilities.name: fs.write
capabilities.description: Create or modify local state non-destructively. Effect::WriteLocal, drawing against the file-operation budget.

capabilities.name: fs.destructive
capabilities.description: Irreversibly remove or overwrite local state. Effect::Destructive, which decide() resolves to Approve in agent mode.

capabilities.name: process.exec
capabilities.description: Execute an arbitrary external command. Effect::Exec, which decide() resolves to Approve in agent mode.

capabilities.name: process.control
capabilities.description: Affect other processes — signal, kill. Effect::Process, which decide() resolves to Approve in agent mode and draws against the process budget.

capabilities.name: ai.complete
capabilities.description: Complete a prompt. Routed to IronGate, which owns model selection, escalation, budget ceilings, and circuit breaking; AetherShell never addresses an inference engine directly.

capabilities.name: ai.model_store
capabilities.description: List, inspect, and convert local model artifacts. Delegated to the IronVault `iv` CLI, so it carries Effect::Exec and is governed as an external command.

capabilities.name: agent.run
capabilities.description: Run an autonomous agent or swarm. Reaches shell.eval, so it inherits its authority and is bounded by the wall-clock and operation budgets.

capabilities.name: session.rewind
capabilities.description: Capture what a mutating call overwrites and rewind it. Reversible sessions are how a destructive step becomes recoverable rather than merely approved.

note: requires_grant is not hand-assigned: it mirrors safety.rs's decide(), where Effect::{Process, Destructive, Exec} resolve to Decision::Approve in agent mode. Effect::Privileged resolves to Decision::Deny and therefore appears as no capability at all — AetherShell refuses that class rather than gating it. Every capability is budgeted except the two that cannot run away: shell.introspect is Effect::Pure, and its catalog is a compile-time table.
